Modern.brandNameRationale: Two words. The third room is the older studio idea: a space that isn't your office and isn't your home, where the actual creative work happens. The brand sits on the room itself, not the deliverable or the discipline.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern creative agencies are competing on portfolio and people. The big network agencies are losing share to smaller, design-led studios with stronger points of view. Brand is doing more work than ever for the agency itself.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Pentagram (pentagram.com) sets the global benchmark. Wolff Olins (wolffolins.com) holds the strategy-led peer position. Mother Design (motherdesign.com) does the personality-forward end. Order (order.design) sits closer in tone. We sit nearest Order in posture.
Modern.positioningStatement: A design studio for founders who want to be in the room, not the email thread.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 50. Founders, COOs, and CMOs at companies of 10 to 500 employees. They've worked with at least one agency before and were unhappy with at least part of it. They want the principal in every meeting.

dos: Show the work, then the process
Name the principal on every project
Speak to the founder, not the marketing department
donts: Photograph the studio empty at golden hour

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark only. THIRD ROOM in a precise modern grotesk, all caps, two words on one line. A small geometric mark, three thin horizontal lines stacked, used as a meta-mark on every project page, the email signature, and the studio's brass plaque.

typography.primary: GT America for the wordmark and major type
typography.secondary: GT America Mono for project metadata and credits
typography.rationale: One family. The mono carries the credits and the project facts. The regular carries the brand.

customSections.title: What it doesn't do
customSections.body: No award-show submissions for projects we wouldn't show our families. No press releases. No 'agency of record' relationships. No social-media-only campaigns.

customSections.title: Where it lives
customSections.body: A studio site that loads the work, not the about page. A printed annual review of the year's projects mailed to clients past and present. A small open studio day twice a year. No paid advertising of the studio itself, ever.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: Two surnames, joined by an ampersand. The structure of a small heritage advisory firm. Wexler and Heath sound like two real partners, the kind whose names are on the door. The whole name reads as a quiet brand consultancy already known to the people who matter.
Luxury.story: Wexler & Heath began with two principals who had each spent fifteen years inside large network agencies and wanted to take fewer clients, more carefully. The firm accepts a small number of engagements each year. Some clients have been with the firm since it opened.
Luxury.industrySummary: Top end brand advisory has been consolidating into larger holding companies. There's a parallel market for small, principal-led firms with deep client relationships. Few clients, long engagements, decades-long retention. The customer is paying for the partners, not the agency machine.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Pentagram (pentagram.com) is the global benchmark. Wolff Olins (wolffolins.com) holds the network-scale strategy peer position. Sullivan (sullivannyc.com) sits closer in tone. We belong in their company on the smaller, more discreet side.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A small brand advisory firm with two partners and twelve clients.

targetAudience.primary: CEOs and founders at mature companies, foundations, and family-held businesses. Hiring brand counsel that will work directly with the principal for years. Not chasing case studies.

dos: Speak in the language of the principal's industry, not ours

Luxury.logoDirection: A classical serif wordmark with elegant ligatures. A small hand-drawn ampersand becomes the firm's hallmark, used on letterhead, embossed business cards, and the brass plaque outside the office. The mark stays small in every application.

colorPalette.name: Counsel Green
colorPalette.meaning: Old leather, library walls, the partner's room.

typography.primary: Canela for the wordmark and printed material
typography.rationale: A high contrast classical serif sets the heritage tone. A modern grotesk handles the few digital surfaces. Both restrained.

customSections.title: What it doesn't do
customSections.body: No public client list. No case studies on the website. No social media presence. No conference appearances. No press.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Two words. Studio One is the most basic name a design studio can have: just the noun and the cardinal number. The brand puts the room and the rank in the brand position. Plain. Honest. Nothing else to say.
Minimal.industrySummary: Agencies have elaborate names, hidden meanings, and origin stories. There's an opening for one that strips it back to the work itself. One studio. One number. Many projects.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Most studios fail this purity test. The closest spirit is Bibliothèque Design's discipline applied with even more restraint, or the early M/M Paris position before the founders became the brand.
Minimal.positioningStatement: A design studio that doesn't have a brand of its own.

targetAudience.primary: Clients who care about the work, not the agency's marketing. They check the portfolio, not the about page. They reorder when the relationship works.

donts: Brand the studio with a story

Minimal.logoDirection: A wordmark only. STUDIO ONE in a single weight grotesk, wide kerned, all caps, two words on one line. No icon. The proposal, the contract, and the final files all carry the same wordmark in the same place.

typography.rationale: One face. The proposal, the deliverable, and the invoice all carry the same wordmark and the same type.

customSections.title: Not this
customSections.body: No agency awards strategy. No newsletter. No manifesto. No conference speaking. No founder-led content.

Corporate.brandNameRationale: Beacon suggests guidance, navigation, and a point of reference. Marketing Group names the category. The whole name reads like a real, established marketing-services firm, the kind already on the procurement panel at Fortune 500 marketing departments.
Corporate.industrySummary: Enterprise marketing services is a multi-billion-dollar B2B category dominated by the big holding companies (WPP, Omnicom, IPG, Publicis). Their interfaces and operating models have aged. There's an opening for a mid-size firm that wins on operational discipline and modern reporting.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: WPP (wpp.com) is the global giant. Accenture Song (accenture.com/song) holds the consulting-led peer. Stagwell (stagwellglobal.com) sits in the modern-holding tier. We sit smaller than any of them, focused on the mid-market enterprise client.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Marketing services for mid-market enterprise companies that have outgrown the holding-company model.
Corporate.positioningRationale: Mid-market companies are too small for the holding company sweetheart treatment and too large for the boutique studio bandwidth. We sit between them, with operating discipline and the responsiveness of a smaller firm.

targetAudience.primary: CMOs and VPs of Marketing at companies of 500 to 10000 employees. They sign annual contracts. They have a board to answer to.
motivations: Reliable delivery without the holding company drag
Reporting that connects marketing to revenue
One contract across creative, media, and measurement

dos: Show case studies with attribution data
donts: Promote individual creative work on social

messagingPillars.name: Outcome-led
messagingPillars.description: Marketing measured against pipeline, revenue, and brand equity. Reported quarterly.

messagingPillars.name: Mid-market specialist
messagingPillars.description: Built for the company that has outgrown its in-house team but isn't ready for a holding company contract.

messagingPillars.name: One contract across services
messagingPillars.description: Creative, paid media, analytics, and CRM under one engagement and one principal.

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark with a small geometric mark to the left. The mark is a single beacon-shape, two triangles meeting at their points to suggest signal and direction. Reads cleanly on a procurement deck, a name badge, and the trust center.

typography.primary: Inter for marketing and B2B materials
typography.secondary: Source Serif Pro for printed quarterly reports
typography.rationale: Inter scales clean across digital. The serif handles formal quarterly business reviews and printed case studies.

customSections.title: What it doesn't do
customSections.body: No celebrity-led creative campaigns. No spec work. No award-show submissions for the firm itself. The firm sells through enterprise marketing procurement, not industry awards.

Creative.brandNameRationale: Two words. Hard Copy is the agency term for the printed version of a deliverable, before digital. Internet slang for the original. The pair gives the studio a double meaning: craft and authenticity. Loud, sharp, and on the customer's tongue already.
Creative.manifesto: Most creative studios sand the edges off their work to make the client comfortable. We made Hard Copy because the work that lasts is the work that landed first and stayed. We sell the original idea, the one before the focus group, the one the client almost killed. We are not a safe agency. We are not for every client. We are for the ones who can recognize the hard copy.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative agency brand has been cautious and clean. There's room for a studio that's loud, opinionated, sticker-friendly, and still produces work that holds up under criticism.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Mother Design (motherdesign.com) holds the personality-forward studio position. Athletics (athletics.com) does the design-led-with-attitude middle. Order (order.design) sits closer in tone. We are sharper than all of them.
Creative.positioningStatement: A creative studio that pitches the original idea, not the safe one.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 50. Founders, CMOs, and Creative Directors who are tired of holding-company work. They want a studio that will fight for the right answer, not the easy one.

dos: Show the original idea, not the one that shipped
Quote the brief and the rejection both
Make jokes about the agency industry
donts: Sand the edges off the work in case studies
Use the word strategic in a sentence with the word activation
Apologize for being a small studio

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark in a punchy display serif with the C of COPY stylized as a small carriage-return mark, suggesting the original typed manuscript. Standalone carriage-return icon for stickers, social profiles, and the back of every printed proposal.

colorPalette.name: Ink
colorPalette.usage: Body type, structure, wordmark on light

typography.primary: Migra for the wordmark and big display
typography.secondary: PP Neue Montreal for body and proposals
typography.rationale: Migra has personality and weight. Neue Montreal keeps the deliverables legible. The pair feels both designed and a little defiant.

customSections.title: What it isn't
customSections.body: Not a holding company. Not an awards-driven studio. Not afraid of red. Not too cool to argue with a client.

customSections.title: Where it lives
customSections.body: Proposals printed on real paper, mailed to the client. Stickers in every project box. A small studio bar that's open the first Friday of every month. A printed yearbook of the past year's work, including the killed ideas.
